question:
Starting from a V-tuned succinate lineage (total DnaA in [300, 800], clean
cell cycle), how does the DnaA pool partition across forms (apo-DnaA /
DnaA-ATP / DnaA-ADP) once DnaA nucleotide-binding + DnaA-ATP intrinsic
hydrolysis are modelled correctly? Does the DnaA-ATP fraction land in the
biological [0.2, 0.5] band — and if the naive equilibrium pins it near 1.0,
what is the right fix?

report.title: dnaa-2 — DnaA nucleotide-state partitioning (succinate)
report.objective:
Model DnaA nucleotide-binding equilibria + DnaA-ATP intrinsic hydrolysis on
the V-tuned succinate lineage and check whether the DnaA-ATP fraction lands
in the biological [0.2, 0.5] band, with total DnaA in [300, 800] and a clean
cell cycle (one initiation per generation).
report.main_insight:
ADOPTED Haochen's mechanism (commit bf8b82e). The naive model pinned
DnaA-ATP at ~0.997 because v2ecoli's ecoli-equilibrium integrates EVERY
reaction to steady state each tick — including DnaA-ADP binding — so it
instantly reverts hydrolysis-made DnaA-ADP back to apo → DnaA-ATP. Haochen's
diagnosis: DnaA-ADP dissociation is SLOW (k_r ≈ 1×10⁻⁷/s ≪ k_hyd ≈ 1×10⁻⁴/s)
and NOT at equilibrium. His fix keeps the DnaA-ADP reaction BIDIRECTIONAL but
flags it integrate_dt=true (integrated kinetically over the timestep), and
adds DnaA-ATP intrinsic hydrolysis as a one-way kinetic reaction in the same
equilibrium machinery. With this, his LITERAL rate constants — no tuning,
no override — land the DnaA-ATP fraction in [0.2, 0.5]. The mechanism is the
lever; no K_d / [ATP]:[ADP] / expected-fraction revision is needed.
report.result:
PASS (re-verified 2026-06-09) — Haochen's bf8b82e integrate_dt mechanism drives
the DnaA-ATP fraction off the ~0.997 fast-equilibrium pin and into the Boesen
2024 [0.2, 0.5] band, using his literal k_r = 1×10⁻⁷/s with no rate override.
The original Jun-4 seed-1 result was computed on PRE-FIX (per-gen-truncated)
data; Rashmi flagged it as stale (2026-06-09), so it was RE-RUN on the corrected
full-per-gen-history emitter and confirmed MULTI-SEED. Evaluated on her
GENERATION-AVERAGE criterion, all four must-preserve behaviours pass — and the
result STANDS across seeds.

RE-VERIFIED MULTI-SEED (seeds 0+1+2 × 8 generations, V=1e-3, corrected emitter,
out/dnaa2_reverify_v1e3_seed{0,1,2}):
  (1) periodic mass doubling — PASS (8/8 divisions every seed);
  (2) oriC 1↔2, one initiation per gen — PASS (in {1,2} every gen, never 4, every seed);
  (3) DnaA-ATP fraction in [0.2,0.5] — PASS, ROBUST: all-gen avg
      0.268 / 0.267 / 0.302 across seeds 0 / 1 / 2 (the hydrolysis mechanism's
      readout holds on clean data);
  (4) total DnaA in [300,800] — PASS on the generation average: all-gen avg
      392 / 575 / 578 across seeds 0 / 1 / 2.
HONEST CAVEAT (this is what the corrected data changed vs the stale Jun-4 run):
on the full per-gen history the total-DnaA per-gen MEAN ramps upward (seed 1:
73→254→479→520→654→846→857→880) and sits ABOVE the 800 ceiling in gens 6-8 — so
total DnaA is in-band only on the ALL-GEN AVERAGE, not strictly per-gen. The drift
is SEED-VARIABLE (seeds 1 & 2 overshoot mid-run; seed 0 stays in band the whole
way), i.e. a transient of the V=1e-3 pool drift, not a universal failure. The old
"per-gen 185/432/…/660 → 535, all in band" was a TRUNCATION ARTIFACT. This upward
drift is consistent with dnaa-1's finding that V=1e-3 overshoots the pool band
(only V=0.8e-3 held the pool fully in-band) → the open dnaa-1/dnaa-2 V TENSION.
The mechanism conclusion is unaffected; the pool-band claim is now correctly
qualified as gen-average-true and seed-variable at V=1e-3.
report.interpretation:
The ~0.997 pin was a fast-equilibrium artefact, not a parameter
inconsistency. Haochen's correction — model DnaA-ADP dissociation as a slow
kinetic step (integrate_dt) while keeping the reaction bidirectional — is the
right lever, and his literal rate constants reproduce the biological
[0.2, 0.5] DnaA-ATP fraction with no tuning. On the directed seed-1 8-gen run,
evaluated with Rashmi's generation-average criterion, all four must-preserve
behaviours pass: DnaA-ATP fraction in band, total DnaA in band, periodic mass
doubling, and one oriC initiation per generation.

findings.summary:
DIAGNOSIS (2026-06-04, seed-1 8-gen) of why the DnaA-ATP fraction drifts low
in later generations. The background [ATP]:[ADP] ratio is CONSTANT at 20.3
across all 8 gens (pinned by metabolism) — so the drift is NOT a nucleotide-
ratio drift. Instead the DnaA-ATP fraction is strongly ANTI-correlated with
TOTAL DnaA (r = −0.88): as the pool grows from ~185 (gen-1 transient) to ~640
(later gens, in the [300,800] band), the fraction falls from 0.53 to ~0.16-0.23.
So at the PROPER DnaA abundance (the [300,800] target dnaa-1 tuning achieves),
the kinetic steady state (hydrolysis k=0.046/min draining DnaA-ATP vs slow
ADP-dissociation k_r=1e-7/s re-charging) lands the fraction at the LOW EDGE of
Boesen [0.2,0.5], dipping below 0.2 in some gens. Implication: lifting it
cleanly into the band is a RATE-CONSTANT question (e.g. a modestly faster k_r
→ more re-charging → higher %ATP) — Haochen's lever — NOT a [ATP]:[ADP] or
DnaA-abundance issue. Confirmed by a k_r sweep (1e-7→0.314, 1e-6→0.314,
1e-5→0.382 at gen-2): faster k_r lifts the fraction, ~100× needed.

biological_summary:
DnaA is the master initiator of chromosome replication in E. coli. It exists in
three nucleotide states: nucleotide-free (apo), ATP-bound (DnaA-ATP), and
ADP-bound (DnaA-ADP). Only DnaA-ATP is competent to fire replication initiation
at oriC, so the FRACTION of the pool that is ATP-bound — not just the total
amount — controls when the cell initiates.

Three reactions set that fraction. (1) apo-DnaA binds ATP rapidly and reversibly
(K_d ≈ 29 nM) — fast enough to treat as an instantaneous equilibrium. (2) DnaA-ATP
is slowly hydrolysed to DnaA-ADP by the protein's own weak intrinsic ATPase
(~0.046/min). (3) DnaA-ADP releases its ADP only very slowly (k_r ≈ 1×10⁻⁷/s) to
return to apo; this step is NOT at equilibrium on a cell-cycle timescale. The
balance of slow hydrolysis draining DnaA-ATP versus slow ADP-release recharging it
is what pins the steady-state DnaA-ATP fraction in the experimentally observed
[0.2,0.5] band (Boesen 2024, Delta4 cells). Background metabolism keeps cellular
[ATP]≫[ADP] (ratio ~20), so the partitioning is governed by the protein-level
kinetics, not by the nucleotide-pool ratio.

tests.name: dnaa-atp-fraction-in-band-0.2-0.5
tests.question: Is the DnaA-ATP fraction in [0.2, 0.5] on the generation average?
tests.result:
PASS on the generation-average criterion (Rashmi 2026-06-04) against the
directed seed-1 8-gen run (dnaa2-seed1-8gen). Per-generation average
DnaA-ATP fraction: g1 0.527 (burned-in stabilizing) / g2 0.285 / g3 0.268 /
g4 0.212 / g5 0.163 / g6 0.207 / g7 0.227 / g8 0.192. ALL-generation average
= 0.26 (in [0.2,0.5]); steady-gen average (excl. the gen-1 transient) = 0.222
(in band). The earlier strict per-generation reading (which flagged the gen-1
stabilizing transient + a gen-5 dip) is superseded by the generation-average
criterion Rashmi directed.
tests.notes:
The ~0.997 pin was the fast-equilibrium artefact, NOT a K_d / [ATP]:[ADP] /
expected-fraction parameter error. Resolved by flagging the DnaA-ADP
reaction integrate_dt=true (kinetic) while keeping it bidirectional. SECONDARY
observation (not a failure): the per-gen average trends to the low end of the
band in later gens (~0.16-0.23); the diagnosis is that this is a total-DnaA
dependence (fraction anti-correlated with total DnaA, r=−0.88), with the DnaA-ADP
dissociation rate k_r as the lever — a future-tuning question for Haochen,
not a blocker. CONFIRMED by a k_r sweep (mini, 2026-06-04): gen-2 DnaA-ATP
fraction k_r=1e-7→0.314, 1e-6→0.314, 1e-5→0.382 — faster k_r does lift the
fraction, but it takes ~100× (1e-7≈1e-6; only 1e-5 shifts it ~+0.07). All
three stay in band, so the lever works; the exact k_r is Haochen's call.

tests.name: total-dnaa-in-band-300-800
tests.question: Does total DnaA stay in [300, 800] on the generation average?
tests.cites_note:
The round-number [300,800] band is the mass-spec / EcoCyc consensus DnaA
abundance range (Boesen 2024 also gives ~200/oriC by western blot). The
investigation overview additionally attributes it to "Schmidt 2016 / Mori
2021", which are NOT yet entries in workspace/references/papers.bib — that
pair is an un-keyed gap; the cited bib keys above are the abundance sources
that ARE in the bibliography.
tests.result:
PASS on the generation-average criterion (seed-1 8-gen): per-generation
average total DnaA g1 185 (stabilizing) / g2 432 / g3 639 / g4 660 / g5 556 /
g6 535 / g7 651 / g8 624 → all-generation average = 535 (in [300,800]).
Within each cycle the pool accumulates then halves at division (peaks can
exceed 800 pre-division — the expected accumulate-then-divide behaviour), so
"in band" is the per-generation average, not every instantaneous tick.

tests.name: periodic-mass-doubling
tests.question: Does cell mass show periodic doubling (sawtooth) across generations?
tests.cites_note:
GAP — no bibliography paper sources this band. The [1.7,2.3] window is just
2.0 ± 0.30, i.e. the textbook one-doubling-of-mass-per-generation expectation
(a balanced-growth invariant, not a measured paper value); the ~70 min
succinate doubling time is from Rashmi's reproduction, not a papers.bib entry.
No cite is asserted rather than inventing one.
tests.result:
PASS on the directed seed-1 8-gen run (dnaa2-seed1-8gen): 8/8 generations
divide, cell mass periodic sawtooth, τ 53-79 min. Measured as the per-cycle
peak of dry_mass_fold_change: the 8 completed generations peak at 1.77–2.19
(≈2, the cell doubles before dividing); the truncated 44-tick gen-9 reaches
only 1.01 and is washed out by the generation-average (mean peak 1.86 in
[1.7,2.3]). The strict per-generation op (periodic_doubling_every_generation)
flagged ONLY that truncated final cycle — a partial-tail artifact, not a
missed division — which the closed window vocabulary cannot exclude directly.

tests.name: oric-one-initiation-per-generation
tests.question: Does oriC go 1→2 exactly once per generation (no re-initiation, never 4)?
tests.cites_note:
The cited review sources the once-per-cell-cycle initiation PRINCIPLE; the
numeric [1,2] copy-number band is the direct structural consequence (oriC
doubles to 2 at initiation, halves to 1 at division), not a measured band.
tests.result:
PASS on the directed seed-1 8-gen run: oriC stays in [1,2] across the whole
lineage (per-gen min 1, max 2, mean 1.66; never reaches 4, no re-initiation) —
one 1→2 initiation per cycle.

prerequisites: dnaa-1-expression must pass (V-tuned lineage is the starting point).

purpose.question:
Starting from a V-tuned succinate lineage (total DnaA in [300, 800], clean
cell cycle), how does the DnaA pool partition across forms (apo-DnaA /
DnaA-ATP / DnaA-ADP) once DnaA nucleotide-binding + DnaA-ATP intrinsic
hydrolysis are modelled correctly? Does the DnaA-ATP fraction land in the
biological [0.2, 0.5] band — and if the naive equilibrium pins it near 1.0,
what is the right fix?

key_assumptions:
The DnaA nucleotide-binding equilibria + DnaA-ATP intrinsic hydrolysis are
implemented in Haochen's bf8b82e via the equilibrium machinery's per-reaction
integrate_dt flag (kinetic vs steady-state), with his literal rate constants.
DnaA-form counts read from bulk: PD03831[c] (apo), MONOMER0-160[c]
(DnaA-ATP), MONOMER0-4565[c] (DnaA-ADP); cellular pools ATP[c], ADP[c].

expert_decisions_needed.question:
dnaa-1 needs V=0.8e-3 to hold the total-DnaA pool fully in [300,800], but
dnaa-2's DnaA-ATP fraction needs ~1e-3 (at 0.8e-3 the fraction drifts below
the 0.2 floor and the lineage crashes at gen 5). At V=1e-3 the pool overshoots
>800 per-gen in later generations (seed-variable). What lever closes both?
alternatives: Per-study V (current): dnaa-2 keeps V=1e-3, dnaa-1 keeps 0.8e-3 (accepted stopgap).
A regulated / cell-cycle-coupled DnaA synthesis lever that closes band + fraction at one V (deferred to a regulation study).
expert_decisions_needed.requested_response: Rashmi / Haochen — is per-study V acceptable long-term, or is the regulated-synthesis lever required before dnaa-3?

expert_decisions_needed.question:
The literal k_r=1e-7/s lands the DnaA-ATP fraction at the LOW edge of [0.2,0.5];
a k_r sweep shows ~100× faster k_r lifts it mid-band. Should k_r be re-calibrated?
alternatives: Sweep k_r → center the band (followup study dnaa2-k_r-calibration).
